coherence.reasons: Both documents have the same governing thought, the same three-part executive summary (economics, constraints, path) and the same slide sequence, with the same evidence under each claim. X puts the recommendation in its executive-summary title, where Y uses a generic 'Executive summary' title and bare 'Appendix' and 'Next steps' dividers. Y in turn separates the cross-dock pilot critique from the gate criteria and gives the Reading A/B sensitivity its own slide, so each title carries one idea. These differences offset each other and do not change the logical hierarchy.

judgment.reasons: The recommendations are identical: keep East in 2027, approve Option K, run a capped all-ZIP cross-dock test through holiday and spring peaks, and decide at a Q3 2028 gate with four criteria. Both drop close-to-Central and match the answer key's preferred conclusion R1. Both weigh the same five options against the same five tests, with the same break-evens, the same Reading A/B sensitivity on the cross-dock minimum and the same reversibility argument. Neither weighs any trade-off the other omits.

evidence.reasons: Both hit every required calculation with the same figures: $1.20M incremental cost, $0.10M net saving, 389.6k against 360k capacity, and a 90.3% network SLA. Both correct the 98% versus 96% claim, the confounded renewal claim and the limits of the six-week pilot. Neither has a numerical error I could find. Y shows slightly more of its working on the main slides: the lower-growth capacity sum (164.8k + 210k = 374.8k), the illustrative rural adjustment, and the Reading B all-in costs ($8.04M and $8.35M). X gives the same figures but leaves some derivations to the appendix or to chart values. The difference is marginal.

revision.reasons: Both handle the CEO's hypothesis the same way and in line with the answer key's 'keep with conditions'. Each tests five conditions (three hold, two hold only partly) and refines the view in the same three ways: optimize rather than just retain, capacity rules out only close-to-Central, and keep East through 2029 rather than permanently. Both note that the CEO had not shown East was the cheapest way to meet the SLA and then demonstrate it. There is no substantive difference.

overall.reasons: The two documents are substantively the same analysis, with the same numbers, tests, recommendation, gate criteria and risk treatment. Y lays out a few derivations more explicitly and adds a next-steps table with owners; X is more compact and its executive-summary title states the answer. Neither difference would change what the board decides or how confident it could be, so the gap is negligible.
